operator_role.note: Buyer contracts with LDC under LDC's own agreements; LDC holds distribution rights from providers and passes through the rights it obtained.

economics_model.note: Annual membership fees plus per-corpus licence fees, on data LDC creates for sponsored programmes or holds under distribution agreements; any payment to providers is not published.

who_pays_fee.note: No published operator fee or split on provider sales.

supply_models.note: commissioned_nonexclusive: data produced for government-sponsored programmes is published in the catalogue.

custody_model.note: Web download from LDC's portal or a shipped drive.

transaction_mode.note: Online cart with e-signature; quotes and pro forma invoices on request; some corpus-specific agreements go by fax or email.

public_prices.note: Membership fees public; per-corpus fees behind login.

licence_model.note: Fixed menu by user type (non-member and not-for-profit research-only vs for-profit member commercial); corpus-specific licences override for some sets.

exclusivity_offered.note: Not addressed on any page fetched; LDC itself does not generally take exclusive rights from providers.

public_listing.note: Descriptions, samples and licence names public; fee requires login.

buyer_vetting.note: A licensing account must be tied to an organisation; no further checks published.

versioning.note: New editions get new catalog IDs and the old edition stays listed; licences to data received are perpetual. Whether past buyers get a new edition free is not published.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Providers must describe consent to LDC, but documentation guidelines do not require consent records for buyers and the licence disclaims all warranties; per-corpus documentation not inspected.

contributor_pay_model.note: No page fetched says how speakers, scribes or annotators are paid, or whether providers get royalties.

catalogue_plus_custom.note: Catalog plus data created for sponsored programmes and listed collection/annotation services.

quality_evidence.note: LDC's own QC claim; vendor-stated. The licences disclaim conformity with documentation.

Q1.answer: LDC sells to universities, corporations and government labs, in single-corpus licences or annual memberships; its most-distributed corpora are text and speech (OntoNotes, TIMIT), with images a minor share. Why buyers choose catalogue over custom is not published.

Q2.answer: Providers give LDC a distribution agreement; LDC does not generally take exclusivity, so they can distribute elsewhere, and LDC adds QC and monthly release. No provider economics published.

Q3.answer: Inventory is LDC's own creation, data produced for US-government-sponsored programmes, and contributions from researchers and media organisations under a distribution agreement; LDC passes through the rights it obtained, with corpus-specific licences where providers require them.

Q4.answer: Data made for sponsored programmes is routinely published in the catalogue; how resale rights are carved out of sponsor contracts, and any retroactive term changes, were not found.

Q5.answer: LDC is licensor of record under its own agreements and grants the rights it obtained; data is as-is with no warranty from LDC, providers or authors, and the for-profit member indemnifies LDC.

Q6.answer: Copied to the buyer: web download from LDC's portal, or hard drive/USB for very large corpora.

Q7.answer: Providers must tell LDC about IRB approval and consent elements, including consent to sharing in a corpus; nothing published shows that evidence passing to the buyer, and the licences disclaim warranties. Property/place owners not addressed.

Q8.answer: Research-only for non-members and not-for-profits, commercial use for for-profit members, perpetual, site-limited, no redistribution; some corpora need signed user agreements kept on file for LDC inspection. No fingerprinting published.

Q9.answer: Self-serve cart with e-signed licences, card/check/wire, or quotes and purchase orders; LDC sets prices (memberships USD 2,400 to 40,000 a year, per-corpus fees behind login).

Q10.answer: A corpus is a catalog item with a catalog number and DOI, released monthly; memberships entitle to a membership year's releases; new editions get new IDs and old ones stay listed. What past buyers get on a new edition is not published.

Q11.answer: Listings show a description, licence name and free sample files; LDC claims its own QC, but the licences disclaim accuracy and conformity with documentation.

Q12.answer: The LDC Catalog is the off-the-shelf side; bespoke work is done as sponsored programmes and listed services, and virtually all sponsored-programme data flows into the Catalog.
